Program: Sector Bridge Apprenticeship Initiative
Award Amount: One Million Two Hundred Fifty Thousand and 00/100 Dollars ($1,250,000.00 USD)
Period of Performance: July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2028
Grant Officer: Renata Colquitt, Workforce Innovation Division
Date of Award: May 19, 2026

The State of Cascadia Office of Economic Opportunity ("the Office") awards the above grant to the Recipient subject to the General Conditions and the Special Conditions set forth in this document. Acceptance of any payment under this award constitutes acceptance of all conditions.

PART A. PROGRAM DESCRIPTION AND DELIVERABLES

A.1 The Recipient shall establish and operate registered apprenticeship pathways in advanced manufacturing and building trades serving residents of Halloway, Deshutes, and Marin Bay counties.

A.2 The Recipient shall enroll not fewer than 180 apprentices during the Period of Performance and shall achieve a twelve-month retention rate of not less than 72 percent.

A.3 The Recipient shall execute employer partnership agreements with not fewer than 22 employers, each committing to at least two apprenticeship placements.

A.4 The Recipient shall deliver a written apprenticeship curriculum package, including competency maps and assessment instruments, to the Office no later than November 30, 2026.

PART B. PRIOR APPROVAL REQUIREMENTS

B.1 General Rule. The Recipient shall obtain the written prior approval of the Grant Officer before taking any action described in this Part B. Approval by any other person, including a program monitor or technical assistance contractor, is not effective. Oral approvals are not binding on the Office. An action taken without required prior approval may result in the disallowance of the associated costs.

B.2 Budget Revisions Exceeding Ten Percent. The Recipient shall request and obtain written prior approval before making any budget revision that would result in cumulative transfers among approved direct cost categories exceeding ten percent (10%) of the total approved budget, being $125,000.00. Transfers below that cumulative threshold may be made without prior approval but must be reported in the next semiannual progress report. Any transfer into or out of the Participant Support Costs category requires written prior approval regardless of amount.

B.3 Key Personnel Changes. The individuals listed in Part F are designated as key personnel. The Recipient shall obtain written prior approval before replacing any key person, before any key person's committed level of effort is reduced by twenty-five percent (25%) or more, and before any key person is absent from the project for a continuous period exceeding three (3) months. Requests shall include the proposed replacement's resume and a statement of comparable qualifications.

Office of Economic Opportunity — Award COEO-2026-WFD-0442 — Page 2 of 6

Office of Economic Opportunity — Award COEO-2026-WFD-0442 — Page 3 of 6

B.4 Change in Scope. The Recipient shall obtain written prior approval before making any change in the scope or objectives of the project, including the addition or elimination of a target occupation, a change in the counties served, a change in the eligible participant population, or a reduction of more than ten percent (10%) in any numeric deliverable stated in Part A.

B.5 Subawards and Contracts. The Recipient shall obtain written prior approval before issuing any subaward, and before executing any contract for services with a value exceeding fifty thousand dollars ($50,000). Requests shall identify the selected entity, the procurement method used, and the basis for the price.

B.6 Equipment. The Recipient shall obtain written prior approval before purchasing any item of equipment with a unit acquisition cost of ten thousand dollars ($10,000) or more, and before disposing of any such item acquired under this award.

B.7 Carryover of Unobligated Balances. Unobligated balances remaining at the end of the first budget period (June 30, 2027) do not automatically carry forward. The Recipient shall submit a written carryover request no later than August 14, 2027, identifying the amount, the reason for the underspending, and the proposed use of the funds.

B.8 No-Cost Extension. Any request to extend the Period of Performance without additional funds shall be submitted in writing not less than forty-five (45) days before June 30, 2028. Only one no-cost extension, not to exceed twelve (12) months, may be granted.

B.9 Form and Timing of Requests. All prior approval requests shall be submitted in writing through the Cascadia Grants System not less than thirty (30) days before the proposed effective date, shall cite the applicable subsection of this Part B, and shall be signed by the Recipient's authorized representative. The Office will ordinarily respond within twenty (20) business days. Silence does not constitute approval.

PART C. REPORTING

C.1 Semiannual Progress Report. The Recipient shall submit a semiannual progress report covering each six-month period of the Period of Performance, due within thirty (30) days after the end of the period. The first semiannual progress report, covering July 1 through December 31, 2026, is due January 30, 2027. Each report shall include enrollment counts, retention data, employer partnership status, budget-to-actual expenditures by category, and disclosure of all budget transfers made under Part B.2.

Office of Economic Opportunity — Award COEO-2026-WFD-0442 — Page 3 of 6
[[PAGE]]
Office of Economic Opportunity — Award COEO-2026-WFD-0442 — Page 4 of 6

C.2 Annual Expenditure Report. An annual expenditure report reconciled to the Recipient's audited general ledger shall be submitted by September 28, 2027 for the first budget period and by September 28, 2028 for the second budget period.

C.3 Final Report. A final programmatic and financial report shall be submitted no later than September 28, 2028, and shall include cumulative performance against every deliverable in Part A, a complete accounting of expenditures, and a list of equipment acquired with award funds.

PART D. PAYMENT AND FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT

D.1 Payments will be made by monthly reimbursement of allowable costs actually incurred and paid. The Office does not provide advance payments under this program.

D.2 The Recipient shall maintain a financial management system that permits the tracking of expenditures by approved budget category and that supports the reporting required in Part C.

D.3 Costs incurred before July 1, 2026, or after June 30, 2028, are unallowable and will not be reimbursed.

D.4 The following costs are unallowable under this award without regard to any prior approval: entertainment, alcoholic beverages, lobbying, fundraising, bad debts, and fines or penalties.

PART E. MONITORING, RECORDS, AND CLOSEOUT

E.1 The Office will conduct at least one desk review and one on-site monitoring visit during the Period of Performance. The Recipient shall make personnel and records available and shall respond to any monitoring findings within thirty (30) days of receipt of the monitoring report.

E.2 The Recipient shall retain all records relating to this award for six (6) years following submission of the final report required by Section C.3.

E.3 The Office will initiate closeout upon acceptance of the final report. Any unexpended or disallowed funds shall be remitted to the Office within forty-five (45) days of the closeout letter.
